h1: Kingston Heat Pump Rebates 2026: Central Hudson
lead: What Kingston homeowners can really get in 2026, checked against Central Hudson and NYSERDA on October 3, 2026.
cards_heading: What you can claim in Kingston in 2026
cards_intro:
Short answer: In Kingston, the main heat pump rebate is NYS Clean Heat (run by Central Hudson): up to $12,000 (Weatherized Tier, old system removed) for a whole-home system, taken off your contractor’s bill. It is one rebate, not several that add up. Lower-income households can get much more through EmPower+, and the federal tax credits ended on December 31, 2025.

after_cards: These are single-family amounts. Apartments and homes under 1,000 sq ft get about half ($2,000 / $3,500 / $1,000, or $4,000 / $6,000 in the Weatherized Tier). Central Hudson’s table does not list a separate DAC column, and its cap is 85% of cost.
sections:
Kingston is the Ulster County seat and is served by Central Hudson. Outside the gas lines, a lot of homes heat with oil or propane; replacing that system entirely is what earns Central Hudson’s larger $7,000 tier ($12,000 in the Weatherized Tier).

Kingston has one of the oldest housing stocks in the state, including stone houses in the Stockade District. Thick masonry walls hold heat well but make running lines for ductless units harder, so expect a longer install.

Historic-district rules may affect where equipment goes on street-facing walls, so check with the city before you sign.

Clean Heat is the Central Hudson rebate, so never add the two together. Clean Heat is capped at 70% of cost (85% in a DAC). There is no separate federal HEAR cheque: New York delivers it through EmPower+. The federal 25C/25D tax credits ended December 31, 2025.

Income-qualified? EmPower+ can cover far more than the utility rebate. Check the state DAC map too: it can raise your amount.
claim_heading: What to do next in Kingston
claim_steps: If you are in a historic district, check the rules for outdoor units.
Get quotes that remove your oil or propane system for the higher tier.
Get 2–3 quotes and ask each contractor to show the rebate tier on the quote.
faq: How much is the heat pump rebate in Kingston?

NYS Clean Heat (run by Central Hudson) pays up to $12,000 (Weatherized Tier, old system removed) for a whole-home heat pump in Kingston, depending on home size, whether you remove the old system, and DAC status.
Can I put a heat pump on a historic Kingston house?
Yes. The rebate is the same; the install may need to keep outdoor units out of sight from the street. Check the city's historic district rules before you sign.
Is the federal tax credit still available for heat pumps?
No. The federal 25C and 25D credits ended for anything installed after December 31, 2025.

Lower-income owners and renters of 1-4 family homes. Low-income households can get free upgrades up to $12,000 upstate or $14,000 downstate; moderate-income households get 50% covered up to $6,000 upstate or $7,000 downstate.
